title: Improve graceful degradation messages for streaming clients when shedding occurs
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: - Streaming responses now terminate with a structured, consistent error event when overload shedding happens after stream start (instead of abrupt EOF), improving client retries and debuggability.
description:
Context: As part of hot-route capacity protection, we increasingly shed/backpressure best-effort traffic and (in rare cases) may terminate in-flight streams when downstream admission/routing cancels work. Today, if shedding occurs after HTTP headers are written, many clients see a raw connection close (EOF) with no structured error, which is hard to distinguish from network issues and leads to inconsistent SDK behavior (e.g., JSON decode errors, missing request_id, inability to surface overload reason). This PR standardizes the termination semantics for streaming requests (/v1/chat/completions, embeddings where applicable) when a shed/overload decision occurs mid-stream. Goals: (1) provide a deterministic, parseable terminal message for SSE/streaming clients, (2) preserve compatibility with OpenAI-style streaming state machines, (3) improve operator and customer debuggability by including request_id + overload reason code, and (4) keep overhead low and cardinality bounded.

What changed (high-level): We introduced a single, shared "stream termination" path in the API gateway streaming writer. When the gateway or routing layer surfaces a ShedError/AdmissionCancelled after streaming has started, we now emit a terminal SSE event with a standardized error payload (aligned with our 429 reason codes) and then close the stream gracefully. For compatibility, we continue to emit the standard terminal marker ("[DONE]") after the error event, so clients that require a terminal sentinel can complete their state machines. We also added explicit safeguards to avoid double-termination, and we ensure the server always flushes the final frames before closing.

New streaming termination behavior: For responses with Content-Type: text/event-stream (stream=true), on mid-stream shedding we emit: (a) an SSE message with event: error and data containing a structured JSON error object including code, message, type, request_id, and redwood_overload fields (reason, retry_after_ms, tier_class), and then (b) a final data: [DONE] line. The error payload is intentionally low-cardinality; it does not include tenant_id/account_id and does not include dynamic tokens/sequence lengths. Example emitted frame (illustrative): event: error\ndata: {"error":{"type":"overload","code":"overload_shed","message":"Request terminated due to capacity protection. Please retry with backoff.","request_id":"req_...","retry_after_ms":750,"redwood":{"reason":"admission_control","tier_class":"best_effort","route_group":"chat.completions"}}}\n\n
Headers/trailers note: We cannot reliably add or mutate HTTP response headers once the stream is in-flight. To support debugging, request_id is always included in the error payload, and we also include the same reason code used by non-streaming 429s (where available). This avoids relying on trailers (not consistently supported across clients/proxies).

Observability: Added gateway metric redwood.gateway.streaming_termination_total with tags: route_group, tier_class, reason (bounded set, shared with 429 reason codes). Added a structured log line at INFO with request_id, reason, route_group, and a boolean indicating whether [DONE] was emitted. This is intended to help support correlate SUP-18462 style reports with on-call dashboards without exploding cardinality.

Implementation notes: - Added StreamTerminationWriter that is the only owner of writing error + done frames and tracking terminal state. - Normal finish paths (model finish_reason, client disconnect, runtime cancel) remain unchanged. - Shedding paths are triggered from AdmissionCancelled/ShedError surfaced by routing/gateway policies; we translate these into an overload error payload appropriate for streaming. - Ensured we do not send an "error" event for non-overload cancellations (e.g., explicit client abort), and we do not mask genuine 5xx before headers are sent (those still return standard non-stream errors).

Tests: Added unit tests covering: (1) mid-stream ShedError emits exactly one error event + [DONE], (2) no duplicate terminal frames if downstream returns multiple cancellations, (3) client disconnect does not emit error frames, (4) payload shape is stable and JSON serializable. Added a lightweight integration test for an SSE client that asserts the final frames are parseable and that request_id is present.

Rollout: No config changes required. Behavior is gated to stream=true SSE responses. This is expected to reduce customer confusion and support load when capacity protection triggers and aligns with the docs work on 429 reason codes.

References: SUP-18462 (streaming client sees inconsistent termination on shed). Related PRs: pr-27441 (429 reason codes), pr-27427 (admission control using capacity signals).
commits: gateway/streaming: introduce StreamTerminationWriter and terminal state tracking
gateway/errors: map ShedError/AdmissionCancelled to standardized overload error payload for SSE
telemetry: add streaming termination metric + structured log event
tests: add unit + integration coverage for mid-stream shedding termination semantics
cleanup: remove ad-hoc EOF handling and consolidate to shared termination path
ci_checks: integration tests - pass (1 rerun due to flaky network timing)
review_conversation: Ravi Menon: We need to be careful about compatibility here. Do we always emit [DONE]? Some clients treat an error chunk as a terminal condition already. Also, can we guarantee this doesn't break OpenAI-compatible parsers?

Amara Diallo (author): Yes, we emit an SSE 'event: error' with a JSON payload, then we still emit 'data: [DONE]' for compatibility with parsers that require a sentinel. The error payload is not shaped like a normal chunk (to avoid being mistaken as a completion delta). The integration test includes an OpenAI-style event loop to validate it doesn't crash on parsing.

Mina Haddad: Where is ShedError coming from? If routing cancels after gateway started streaming, do we have a single canonical reason code? We should align with the 429 reason set so Support can map it 1:1.

Amara Diallo (author): ShedError reasons are mapped to the same bounded set as our 429 reason codes. For mid-stream we use overload_shed + redwood.reason (admission_control|queue_depth|capacity_floor). I added a small mapping table in gateway/errors/overload_mapping.go and a unit test for each reason.

Logan Wright: Metric tags: do NOT include request path or model name; route_group is fine. Also ensure reason is a bounded enum. Can you add a comment to the metric spec to prevent future regressions?

Amara Diallo (author): Updated tags to (route_group, tier_class, reason) only. Added an inline comment and a lint-style assertion in the metric registration that reason must be one of the known strings.
Peter Holtz: Edge case: if client disconnects while we're writing the error frame, we might log scary errors. Can we downgrade write failures caused by broken pipe?
Amara Diallo (author): Added handling to treat EPIPE/ECONNRESET as expected during termination and keep logs at DEBUG. Unit test covers client abort path.
Elliot Price: Please align the customer-facing message text with the docs language ('retry with exponential backoff', avoid 'noisy neighbor'). Also, include request_id in the payload always.
Amara Diallo (author): Updated message string to match docs phrasing and ensured request_id is populated even when upstream didn't attach headers (falls back to our generated req id).
Ravi Menon: Approved after changes. Thanks for keeping it bounded and deterministic.
